Plot a Heat Map following WJP style guidelines

Source: R/heatmapChart.R
wjp_heatmap.Rd

wjp_heatmap() draws a matrix of colored cells (e.g., the share of people with one problem who also had another), with the printed value of each cell and the column labels at the top.

Usage

wjp_heatmap(
  data,
  x,
  y,
  fill,
  labels = NULL,
  x_order = NULL,
  y_order = NULL,
  cvec = NULL,
  na_fill = "#FFFFFF",
  border_color = "#FFFFFF",
  label_color = "auto",
  x_position = c("top", "bottom"),
  x_angle = 40,
  legend_position = "top",
  border_width = 1.5,
  label_size = 9.5,
  label_fontface = "plain",
  label_dark = "#1A1A1A",
  axis_text_size = 10,
  axis_text_colour = "#1A1A1A",
  x_title = NULL,
  y_title = NULL,
  title_size = 11,
  title_fontface = "bold.italic",
  title_colour = "#575796",
  legend_text_size = 10,
  legend_key_size = NULL,
  legend_fontface = "plain",
  legend_justification = c("left", "center", "right"),
  cell_size = NULL,
  margins = c(9, 41, 9, 9),
  ptheme = WJP_theme()
)

Arguments

data

Data frame containing the data to plot.

x

String. Column name of the variable with the column categories.

y

String. Column name of the variable with the row categories.

fill

String. Column name of the variable that sets the cell color (categorical or numeric).

labels

String. Column name of the variable with the printed values. Default is NULL (no labels).

x_order, y_order

Character vectors with the order of the columns (left to right) and rows (top to bottom). Default is NULL (order of first appearance).

cvec

Colors: named by the fill values (categorical fill) or the low and high ends of the scale (numeric fill). Default is NULL (sequential WJP report colors).

na_fill

String. Color of cells with a missing fill. Default is "#FFFFFF".

border_color

String. Color of the cell borders. Default is "#FFFFFF".

label_color

Color of the labels: "auto" (default; white on dark cells) or one color.

x_position

String. Position of the column labels: "top" (default) or "bottom".

x_angle

Numeric. Angle of the column labels, in degrees. Default is 40.

legend_position

Legend position: "top" (default), "bottom", "left", "right", c(x, y) inside the panel, or "none".

border_width

Numeric. Width of the cell borders, in points. Default is 1.5.

label_size

Numeric. Size of the labels, in points. Default is 9.5.

label_fontface

String. Font face of the labels. Default is "plain".

label_dark

String. Color of the labels on light cells with label_color = "auto". Default is "#1A1A1A".

axis_text_size

Numeric. Size of the row and column labels, in points. Default is 10.

axis_text_colour

String. Color of the row and column labels. Default is "#1A1A1A".

x_title, y_title

Strings. Titles of the columns and rows. Default is NULL (none).

title_size

Numeric. Size of the titles, in points. Default is 11.

title_fontface

String. Font face of the titles. Default is "bold.italic".

title_colour

String. Color of the titles. Default is "#575796".

legend_text_size

Numeric. Size of the legend text, in points. Default is 10.

legend_key_size

Numeric. Size of the legend keys, in points. Default is NULL.

legend_fontface

String. Font face of the legend text. Default is "plain".

legend_justification

String. Horizontal alignment of a top or bottom legend: "left" (default), "center", or "right".

cell_size

Numeric. Side of each (square) cell, in points. Default is NULL (the panel fills the device).

margins

Numeric vector of four margins (top, right, bottom, left), in points. Default is c(9, 41, 9, 9).

ptheme

ggplot theme to apply. Default is WJP_theme().

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

The function expects one row per cell: the column category in x, the row category in y, and the variable that sets the color in fill. Columns are drawn from left to right and rows from top to bottom in order of first appearance, or in the order given by x_order and y_order.

Colors. A categorical fill (character, factor, or logical; e.g., bands such as "Less than 25%") uses cvec, a vector of colors named by the fill values (or given in the order of the levels); by default a sequential ramp from "#E5E8E8" to "#575796" over the levels, in factor order or order of first appearance. A numeric fill uses a sequential scale between cvec[1] and cvec[2] (see scale_fill_wjp_seq()). Cells with a missing fill are drawn in na_fill. With label_color = "auto", labels on dark cells are white.

Labels. The labels column is printed as given (e.g., "62%", "N/A", or a dash on the diagonal). Without it, no value is printed.

Size. With cell_size, cells are squares of that many points and the chart has a definite size for wjp_save(); otherwise the panel fills the device.

Examples

# Always load the WJP fonts
wjp_fonts()

# Share of people with a problem (columns) who also had another (rows)
# (fictional data)
problems <- c("Consumer", "Housing", "Employment")
cooc <- expand.grid(column = problems, row = problems, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cooc$value <- c(NA, 45, 62, 30, NA, 55, 18, 27, NA)
cooc$band <- cut(cooc$value, c(-Inf, 25, 50, Inf), right = FALSE,
                 labels = c("Less than 25%", "25% to 50%", "50% or more"))
cooc$text <- ifelse(is.na(cooc$value), "–", paste0(cooc$value, "%"))

wjp_heatmap(
  cooc,
  x       = "column",
  y       = "row",
  fill    = "band",
  labels  = "text",
  x_title = "Among people who experienced problems with:",
  y_title = "People who also experienced:"
)
